summary.reviewer: AI-assisted visual audit; no independent human annotator adjudication
summary.interpretation: No chess-like prompt/label scope defect found in this reviewed subset. This is a limited spot-check, not certification of the entire dataset.

native_metrics_context.conclusion: Argon is strong at finding/counting pills at IoU 0.5 on these 48. Lower AP50:95 chiefly reflects box-boundary precision plus one schema failure; avoid a claim that it generally fails to see/count pills.

summary.occlusion_convention: Most reviewed objects are fully visible, touching, or only mildly overlapping. Boxes generally bound whole visible pills. The few ambiguous overlaps do not establish a reliable universal amodal/full-shape annotation convention.
limitations: 12 fixed samples plus 6 disagreement-selected images do not estimate dataset-wide annotation error rate.
There was no blinded independent human review or relabeling.
Reflection/background identity and obscured extent are visually inferred.
A display score threshold of 0.25 does not change the native AP evaluation, which retains all scores.
No classes, labels, images, predictions, prompts, thresholds used for scoring, or test selections were changed by this audit.
Model inputs matched local image hashes/dimensions; internal remote-provider preprocessing was not independently observed.
